policy.about: Teach first: each new skill step opens with Professor Hoot modelling one card (I do), one guided card together (we do), then the quiz (you do). Lesson cards never count as evidence, stars or Play Zone time. Times Tables are recited again on the first round of every day.
genericHints: look at the yellow words read them
look at the orange place on the map
think about where each animal lives

phrases.firstSound: I listen to the first sound.
phrases.firstLetter: I look at the first letter.

decodable.about: Reading words must use only spelling patterns the child has been taught. Each pattern stage includes the ones before it. A word with a pattern above its level is left out of that level's pool (reading, listening and spelling cards alike). Grade 1 spelling step 4 and up includes two-syllable picture words, so it is not limited.

stageNames.short: Single letters with their first sound and short vowels (cat, ant, six)
stageNames.digraphs: Two letters, one sound (sh ch th wh ck ng ll ss ff zz qu) and blends (frog, drum, fish)
stageNames.magicE: Silent e makes the vowel say its name (cake, kite, bone)
stageNames.teams: Vowel teams, r-controlled vowels, y as a vowel and welded sounds (rain, tree, star, fly, ball)

tables.about: Times tables ladder, in counting order: the 1 times table, then 2, then 3 ... up to 10, then all tables mixed. Each step is taught first (Professor Hoot reads the whole table aloud, 1 × 1, 1 × 2 ...), then one card together, then the quiz. Younger grades get picture cards (equal groups, what comes next) among the facts, and Kindergarten is quizzed only on answers up to 10.

practice.about: Tables are learned by saying and practising them again and again, over months. A child moves to the next table only after this many strong rounds, on this many different days. Earlier tables keep coming back in every quiz.
